mentions.name: Open Science Archive
mentions.description: Open infrastructure for scientific databases, letting every scientific field spin up its own Protein Data Bank-style archive in one click. Demos are live mirroring/extending PDB and GEO; planned work includes APIs with good developer experience, ML-friendly export, and a unified AI-driven UI that works for all scientific data types.
mentions.problem: Scientific fields lack shared, one-click deployable data archives comparable to the Protein Data Bank.
mentions.audience: Scientific researchers who need field-specific public data archives
mentions.source_excerpt: Open Science Archive: open infrastructure for scientific databases, so that every field gets its own Protein Data Bank in 1-click.

mentions.name: Open Science Archive
mentions.description: A domain-agnostic scientific data archive inspired by the Protein Data Bank. It handles deposition, validation, curation, storage, and searching of scientific data, with plugin interfaces for domain-specific components. Designed as "PDB-in-a-box" so scientific organisations can spin up professional-grade data infrastructure in days, accelerating AI-for-science efforts.
mentions.problem: Setting up professional-grade scientific data infrastructure is slow and difficult, which hampers AI-for-science efforts.
mentions.audience: Scientific organisations that need to stand up professional-grade data infrastructure quickly to support AI-for-science efforts.
mentions.source_excerpt:
https://opensciencearchive.org

I’ve started building a domain-agnostic scientific data archive, inspired by the Protein Data Bank. It handles the deposition, validation, curation, storage, and searching of scientific data, with plugin interfaces for domain-specific components.

The goal is to accelerate AI-for-science efforts by making it easy for scientific organisations to spin-up professional-grade data infrastructure in a matter of days. “PDB-in-a-box”.
